answer.rationale: General caveat first: every memory here is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so none carries effect sizes, sample sizes, confidence intervals, segment definitions, or observation windows. All ratings are therefore ceilinged — I can judge only how close each claim's stated outcome sits to sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not how solid the underlying evidence was. Also worth noting the newest memory is 15 days old and the three current problems (competitor pricing, -6% activation, -4% onboarding) may have shifted the conditions those findings were measured under. Per memory: memory_57 (4) is closest to the objective — it names qualified revenue explicitly and reports an absence of retention harm, i.e. it speaks to both the 'qualified' and 'sustainable' halves; it is weakened by not stating the observation window behind 'no measurable harm' or the incentive cost against the revenue added. memory_44 (4) also targets the objective directly via pipeline quality, a genuine qualified-revenue proxy, but stops at pipeline rather than closed or retained revenue, and says nothing about the cost-to-serve of sales-assisted motion. memory_86 (3) and memory_31 (3) are activation/adoption findings one or two steps upstream of revenue; memory_31 earns its 3 on the word 'durable,' though durability is claimed for activation, not for revenue, and cutting signup fields plausibly trades lead quality for volume — a direct risk to the 'qualified' criterion that the memory does not address. memory_86 is similarly silent on whether faster time-to-value converted into paid expansion or retention. memory_73 (2) is the trap: it is the only memory that names revenue lift and the only one that maps onto the competitor situation, which makes it the tempting pick this week, but promotional pricing evidence without margin, discount-cohort retention, or post-promotion renewal data is nearly uninformative about sustainable revenue — discounted acquisition can raise recorded revenue while lowering lifetime value, and matching a competitor's entry pricing risks a margin race this memory gives no basis to survive. memory_91 (2) is the least supported: week-one engagement and a first meaningful action are the shallowest outcomes in the set, with no durability claim, no retention link, and no revenue link at all. It is the memory whose stated result is furthest from the objective, and its apparent relevance comes only from surface-matching the word 'activation' in the current metrics rather than from evidence about revenue.
